newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house OKs controversial shipping bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house OKs controversial shipping bill.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies approved a bill opening up inland and coastal shipping, an official said.
The bill, which was approved by show of hands in the lower house, will allow foreign shipping lines to operate services between Brazilian ports.

Deputy Jose Carlos Aleliua, who drew up the bill, said the legislation creates a so-called Special Brazilian Regime (REB) effectively allowing foreign shipping lines with an administrative base in Brazil treatment equal to that granted to Brazilian firms.
Any boat seeking REP status must have a Brazilian captain and chief machinist.
Company's who qualify for REP will enjoy exemption from some taxes and worker benefits, he said.
Aleluia said the aim of the bill was to attract foreign companies to Brazil and reduce the cost of transportation.
The bill, which regulates the 1995 opening of the Brazilian inland shipping sector to foreign firms, must now be approved by the Senate.
